newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee nuclear plant review to last 3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee nuclear plant review to last 3 weeks.

text.p: Maine Yankee's review of the cabling at its 910 megawatt (MW) nuclear power station, necessary before the plant can return to service, will likely last well into January, the company said Thursday.
"We expect the review will take about three weeks," said Maine Yankee spokeswoman Maureen Brown.

Maine Yankee officials, in a statement issued earlier Thursday, said they will present a thorough review of the cable separation issues to the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) before restarting of the plant.
The plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, was shut December 6 when workers discovered two improperly installed electrical cables in the reactor control system that did not meet the plant's safety requirements.
The cables serve the reactor trip breakers which are used to shut the plant manually or automatically.

In a letter to the operator, NRC Region I Administrator Hubert Miller said that twice since the plant shut down, Maine Yankee's plan for determining the extent of the cable separation problem had been "insufficient."
The company has since revised its approach to assessing the scope of the problem, NRC said.
NRC said it has sent three specialists to assess the extent of the problem. Results of their findings, to be issued separately from those by the company, will be published early next year, NRC said.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
